humanities_role_explanation: Historical newspaper text (BLN600) supplies the items, but the competence tested is general post-OCR error correction (sequence-to-sequence text repair), not disciplinary humanities competence.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only: OCR output text is mapped to manually re-keyed ground-truth text; images are not given to models.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Post-OCR correction: detecting and correcting OCR errors (substitutions, insertions, deletions, misnamed entities) in 19th century newspaper text, framed as NMT for BART and as prompt-based instruction following for Llama 2.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Single-task study on one dataset (BLN600, post-OCR correction); not a broad multi-task benchmark and no new benchmark is introduced.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Instruction-tuned Llama 2 7B and 13B (LoRA), compared with fine-tuned BART base/large.

quantitative_metrics.note: Percentage reduction in character error rate (CER), based on Levenshtein distance.

summary: The paper adapts generative LLMs to post-OCR correction of 19th century British newspapers by instruction-tuning Llama 2 and comparing it with fine-tuned BART on BLN600. Llama 2 13B reduces CER by 54.51% versus 23.30% for BART large, and Llama 2 does well even with limited training data.
key_findings: Llama 2 13B achieves 54.51% CER reduction, Llama 2 7B 43.26%, BART large 23.30%, BART base 14.60%. Llama 2 performs strongly with small training sets while BART improves with more data. Substitutions and deletions are easiest to correct; insertions and heavily corrupted entities are hardest.
facets_explanation: Reference texts are manually re-keyed human transcriptions of the source images, supplied by the existing BLN600 corpus (Booth et al., 2024). Scoring compares model output to this single ground truth via CER. The paper does not discuss annotator disagreement.
results_explanation: Table 3 reports CER Reduction (%): BART 140M 14.60, BART 400M 23.30, Llama 2 7B 43.26, Llama 2 13B 54.51, each a mean over five training and evaluation iterations. The best score is a percentage reduction in CER, not a standard metric, hence 'other'. No human baseline is reported and a single format is evaluated.

humanities_role.quote: Poor OCR quality continues to be a major obstacle for humanities scholars seeking to make use of digitised primary sources such as historical newspapers.

dataset_size.quote: Comprising 600 samples, the articles are sourced from six different publications

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: By instruction-tuning Llama 2 and comparing it to a fine-tuned BART on BLN600

gold_source.quote: along with high-quality manually re-keyed human transcriptions from the source images

answer_multiplicity.quote: computing the Levenshtein distance between the recognised text and the reference text

reported_best_score.quote: Llama 2 significantly outperforms BART, particularly the 13B model, which is over twice as effective with a score of 54.51%.
